_comment: Adapter-specific declarations for the fleet tooling (Entwicklung/scripts). They live HERE so that a change in this adapter never touches the locked tooling. Readers: sync-iopackage-from-i18n.py (manifestI18n, release gate B03) and submit-stable.py (forumThread). Keys starting with an underscore are comments.

manifestI18n._comment: instanceObjects id -> key in admin/i18n/<lang>.json. Every manifest object needs a `name` entry (an object without one is a structural error, and so is an entry whose object no longer exists); `desc` only where the name does not already say it - an empty desc beats an invented sentence.
manifestI18n._note: The standard objects and the three device counts; the device datapoints are created at runtime (main.ts, tName/tDesc/tRaw).

_deviceIds: Each emulated Roku is a device object whose id comes from the name the user gives it; renaming changes only the displayed name (K3).

deviceIds.userNamed: device name set in the device dialog of the device manager

noDeviceSources: fakeroku is a Roku emulator for remotes such as Logitech Harmony: it controls no devices, it answers as a Roku so the remote's keys can trigger ioBroker scripts, so there are no devices to research or add
_suites: fakeroku has no counterpart (sealed register, krobi 2026-10-02 22:05): it logs in nowhere and no device of its own can drop off. Its devices come from its settings, so the fixture renames one there (test/inventory.js feedFixtures).

connectionTest.none: the settings page has no connection test: fakeroku connects to nothing, the remotes connect to it

groupSwitches.none: no setting adds or removes a group of datapoints: every Roku has its fixed keys

rejectLogin.none: fakeroku logs in nowhere: it is an emulator without a counterpart

dropDevice.none: no counterpart: an emulated Roku runs as long as the adapter runs and never drops off a remote list

serverTest._why: On the real host every emulated Roku listens and discovery runs: the instance is green, every Roku online, the counts are numbers.
serverTest.noCommands: fakeroku switches nothing: its datapoints report what a remote pressed, no command goes to a device

_listenPorts: Every port the adapter opens. `key` is a native key only for primary/secondary; for shared and perDevice it is a label. fakeroku has no primary port: each emulated Roku carries its own ECP port in native.devices[], and SSDP 1900 is shared on purpose (declaring it as native.port would warn every UPnP user on the host).
